doc.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013

title: First concert and plans for graduate school in Canada
summary: The Mangione brothers' show was his first concert, starting his habit of concerts with educational workshops; he planned to play ball and study in Canada.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. So you know that those guys would go for Sunday. They’d say, “You’ve got to make a stop at Rochester, the Mangione family will take good care of you.” So she said — I said, “well let me know something about them. Bring their scrapbook and everything else.” The first concert I ever did was the Mangione brothers. 196 — it was probably ’65 or maybe late ’64. I don’t have any posters of it, but that was the first one I did. And that was the beginning of me putting on concerts and eventually doing things where I would do little workshops with each of the artists. That was the key. You had to be educational. And I came back to Buffalo — so I graduated and I was going to be a writer. I worked for the Courier as a summer sports replacement, and in 1966 I graduated, and I sent to all these Canadian colleges, because they weren’t very good. We’d always play one Canadian college at the beginning of the season. We played Toronto, Western Ontario, and one other one. And those coaches I wrote to and I said I want to do my graduate work in Canada, because I know that I’ll be able to play as a graduate student for two years. This was heaven. I mean there was a high scorer in Western, New York, Conesus, Niagara, the whole bit. So I wasn’t quite good enough to be in the pros, I didn’t have the ABA at the time.
